Small white daisy flowers with yellow centers appear in flushes tied to rainfall from spring through fall, drawing native bees, small butterflies, and skippers to the sparse Chihuahuan Desert grasslands and limestone flats where it naturally grows. It is exceptionally heat- and drought-tolerant once established and essentially maintenance-free, needing no deadheading or supplemental water in its native range. Use it as a durable edging or rock-garden groundcover where nothing else will hold up to reflected heat.

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in fall into lean, sandy or gravelly, sharply drained soil in full sun, ideally against a dry wash or rocky slope similar to its native Mojave and Sonoran Desert habitat.

Bladder sage produces small tubular violet-and-white flowers favored by hummingbirds and native bees, followed by its namesake inflated, papery seed capsules that persist and rattle through summer, adding ornamental interest after bloom. It is a wiry, intricately branched shrub that is nearly leafless in dry periods, an adaptation that makes it extremely drought tolerant once established. Avoid summer irrigation and heavy soils, which quickly cause root rot in this true desert specialist.

planting.note: Plant container stock in fall as Pacific Northwest rains return, into well-drained soil that ranges from dry to moist, in partial shade to full sun near the coast; seed requires 60–90 days cold-moist stratification and germinates slowly and erratically even after chilling.

Oceanspray is a fast-growing, arching native shrub of forest edges and clearings from British Columbia to California, producing long, cascading plumes of tiny cream-white flowers in early summer that cover the shrub in a foam-like display visible from a distance. The abundant bloom is a magnet for native bees, butterflies, and beneficial wasps, and the dense thickets it forms provide excellent cover and nesting habitat for songbirds. It tolerates a wide range of soils and light conditions once established, making it a versatile hedgerow or restoration planting for Pacific Northwest gardens.

planting.note: Plant container-grown coyote brush in fall into well-drained soil in full sun; it tolerates fog, wind, salt spray, clay, and extended drought once established.

directions: Plant container-grown coyote brush in fall into well-drained soil in full sun; it is one of the most adaptable evergreen shrubs of the California coast and coastal ranges, tolerating fog, wind, salt spray, clay, and extended drought once established. Plants are dioecious, and though wind-pollinated, the male and female flowers that appear in late fall are an outsized late-season nectar and pollen source for migrating butterflies, native bees, and beneficial insects at a time when little else is blooming. Low, spreading cultivars are widely used as erosion-control groundcovers on slopes, while the upright species form makes an excellent informal hedge or wildlife screen. It requires essentially no irrigation once established and tolerates hard pruning to control size.

planting.note: Direct sow or set out transplants in fall or early spring into well-drained, sandy soil in full sun, ideal for coastal California and southern Oregon plantings where seaside daisy grows naturally on bluffs and dunes.

Its thick, spoon-shaped, blue-green leaves form low mounding clumps that send up lavender-pink, daisy-like flowers with yellow centers from spring through summer, attracting native bees and small butterflies along the fog-belt coast. It handles salt spray, wind, and sandy, low-fertility soils that few other flowering perennials tolerate, making it a reliable choice for coastal gardens and erosion-control plantings. Deadheading extends bloom, though plants perform well with minimal care once established.
